**Pre-release — not production-ready.**

## Unth Recover v0.1.0-alpha — PostgreSQL recovery proof (M0)

Backs up a PostgreSQL database and **proves it can be recovered**: every `unth verify` restores
the backup into a fresh, isolated PostgreSQL container and compares row counts, table contents,
schema objects, constraints and your own assertion queries with a fingerprint taken in the same
snapshot as the dump. A backup is `VERIFIED` only if all ten mandatory steps pass — a checksum
alone never verifies a backup.

### Included
- `unth version | doctor | discover docker|postgres | backup postgres|list|show | verify | report | cleanup | audit list`
- Snapshot-consistent `pg_dump` backups, SHA-256 + manifest, SQLite metadata, audit trail
- Hardened restore sandbox (internal network, no published ports, dropped capabilities, limits) with label-scoped cleanup
- JSON/text reports with explicit verification scope and RTO/RPO caveats

### Tested
- Integration suite in CI with PostgreSQL **12, 13, 14, 15, 16** (pg_dump 16) and **17** (pg_dump 17), Docker Engine 28/29, Linux x86_64
- The product code of this build is identical to the code tested in that matrix (later commits changed tests, CI and docs only)
- Large database (local): 5M rows / 1.5 GB → backup 16 s, verification 32 s (restore 26 s)
- The release binary itself is smoke-tested on a clean runner by `publish-release.yml`

### Known limitations
- Linux only; restore sandbox requires host access to Docker bridge networks
- Backups are **not encrypted**; SHA-256 checksums are **not signatures**
- Roles, ownership, privileges and cluster settings are not verified
- Scheduling, retention, notifications and Docker volume backups are on `main` (M1) and will ship in `v0.2.0-alpha`

### Install
```bash
curl -fsSLO https://raw.githubusercontent.com/unmadethings/unthrecover/main/scripts/install.sh
sudo sh install.sh --version v0.1.0-alpha
```
Pre-releases are not "latest", so `--version` is required. Manual check: `sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS --ignore-missing`.
